Pickup Truck Popemobiles Headline Pope Leo XIV's South American Visit

ER
By Elena Rostova Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst • via Carscoops Wire
⚡ Visual Story
Source & Photography: Carscoops Wire Dispatch Verified Editorial Asset
⚡ Executive Takeaways & Key Highlights

⚡ EDITORIAL TAKE • ELENA ROSTOVA Global Automotive Industry & Supply-Chain Analyst

Capital Allocation Across Global Automakers

From an institutional perspective, the economic figures outlined in this dispatch from Carscoops reflect monumental shifts in automotive capital. Legacy original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and agile EV startups alike must balance heavy gigafactory capital expenditures against fluctuating consumer demand and trade tariffs. Supply chain resilience—especially across lithium, cathode precursor materials, and semiconductors—is determining profitability.

Big Picture: Upcoming quarterly delivery reports and operating margins will indicate which manufacturers are successfully navigating the EV transformation curve.

The pope left his electric G Wagon in the Vatican, and traveled South America in a trio of custom trucks

📌 The Core Development

The world has seen more Popemobiles than Popes, but some examples are cooler than others, including the Mercedes G Wagon EV . During Pope Leo XIV's recent trip to South America, three automakers and local coachbuilders transformed midsize pickups into open-air ceremonial vehicles. The Pontiff sat on the rear bed of the Toyota Hilux, the Chevrolet S10, and the Fiat Titano. However, the Toyota was the most interesting of the three, with local reports suggesting it is an old chassis wearing the design of the new model.

But let's take it from the start. Toyota Argentina officially presented the Popemobile as a preview of the ninth-generation Hilux . The latest iteration of the popular workhorse debuted globally in November 2025 and is already on sale in Europe, Australia, and South Africa. However, Argentina will get it soon, with local production taking place at the Zárate assembly plant.

🔍 Background & Sector Context

Toyota confirmed that the two donor vehicles for the Popemobiles were manufactured in Argentina. While these could be pre-production prototypes, Motor1 Brazil reports that the project was approved before the end of the summer suggesting that the starting point was the older eight-generation Hilux.

In any case, coachbuilder Vallé Equipamientos did a great job integrating the exterior and interior design of the ninth-generation model alongside the Popemobile-specific modifications. Of course, the fact that the new Hilux retains the hardpoints, greenhouse, pillars, doors, and basic structure of its predecessor helped a lot.

📊 Industry & Real-World Impact

Besides retrofitting the redesigned nose, fender, lights, and interior to the donor vehicle, the coachbuilder applied a number of Pope-specific upgrades "according to the requirements established by the Vatican." The highlight is the illuminated polycarbonate dome covering what used to be the cargo area of the single-cab pickup and increasing its total height to 122 in (3.1 m).

🔮 Strategic Outlook & What Lies Ahead

The rear bed gained a comfy throne, which is upholstered in white eco leather, flanked by two side-facing foldable seats at the back. Access to the rear deck is made possible by custom steps and a cutout on the tailgate. The truck is painted white, with matching cladding all around the bodywork. Diplomatic touches include Vatican fender pennants, Papal coat of arms badging on the profile, and Vatican City State registration plates.

Under the skin, the Hilux retains the IMV ladder-frame chassis and the standard turbodiesel engine. However, the rear leaf springs and the shock absorbers have been recalibrated, to offer a stable and comfortable ride. Toyota Argentina commissioned two identical examples of the Hilux Popemobile to cover the needs of the trip in Buenos Aires and Cordoba, while supplying numerous support vehicles. According to the company, the Hilux was chosen because it's the most produced vehicle in Argentina.
